newsitem.title: USA: US Fed approves NationsBank merger proposal.
newsitem.headline: US Fed approves NationsBank merger proposal.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Reserve on Monday approved a proposal by NationsBank Corp of Charlotte, N.C., to merge with Boatmen's Bancshares Inc of St Louis, Mo.
The merger was opposed by numerous community activist groups that had expressed concern the merged companies would leave low-income neighborhoods underserved.
But the Fed approved the deal unanimously, ruling that the lending records of both companies "are consistent with approval of this proposal."

NationsBank is the fifth-largest bank in the United States and the premier banking power in the Southeast, with assets of about $192.3 billion. Boatmen's is the 24th largest U.S. bank with assets of $40.7 billion.

After the merger with Boatmen's, valued by analysts at around $9 billion, NationsBank will extend its franchise into the U.S. heartland and move up to become the fourth-largest bank in the United States.
NationsBank Chairman Hugh McColl has said previously there will be some layoffs. NationsBank has 67,000 employees and Boatmen's has 17,000.

In a 45-page decision, the Fed said it concluded "consummation of the proposal would not have a significantly adverse impact on competition or the concentration of banking resources in any relevant banking market."
The Fed noted that 15 groups had criticized the lending performance of NationsBank and Boatmen's in lower-income communities.

Recently, about 100 protestors including minority contractors picketed outside the New York Stock Exchange opposing the merger, saying they wanted NationsBank to adopt commitments to minority businesses as a condition of approval.

The Fed said its examiners had reviewed both banks' lending records, which are governed by the Community Reinvestment Act, and cited steps NationsBank has taken to boost lending to minority borrowers.
The proposed merger of NationsBank and Boatmen's was made public last August. They are seeking to complete the transaction in January.

As recently as last week, an activist group called Inner City Press/Community on the Move claimed NationsBank's consumer finance unit charged "predatory" interest rates up to 20 percent "disproportionately to people of color."
A spokeswoman for NationsBank denied the charge, saying the bank had a strong record and a diverse customer base including all races, genders and income levels.
